entries.reason: The only two calls to private paired() pass n from main after rejecting values outside 100..=5000. Two Vec<u128> element capacities are jointly bounded by 160000 bytes. CLI parse failure returns before allocation. No product or query change is justified by the reported unbounded-size claim.

missing() returns Result<bool> used only in the branch condition of Enrollment::signer(). Both branches return a DeviceSigningKey opened/provisioned using the separately loaded JournalKey; the boolean is not serialized or converted to cryptographic bytes. The two named sinks both initialize journal AEAD from key.0.as_bytes(), an opaque JournalKey supplied to the journal. Production JournalKey construction fills all 32 bytes with getrandom or read_exact from the protected key file before returning. The reported taint jump from the branch condition to the returned owner and its journal key is not a concrete key-value flow. All two named sinks and all four supplied traces per result were checked.

The sole reported operation is certificates.remove(0), where certificates has concrete Vec<Vec<u8>> type containing issued public certificates. It removes/drops the local member from an owned vector; it is not a logger, formatting call or output sink. The sole trace starts and ends on this expression.

Both reported send_account_message results reach logging only through Vec::len(). Neither formatted expression passes the result vector, member output or plaintext bytes. The other fields are process-cut labels, boolean fixture mode, fixed sample/size choices and elapsed time. In result588, plaintext length is selected from a fixed boundary-test table and plaintext bytes are synthetic 0x5a, not application input. This is not an endorsement of logging arbitrary production message metadata.

scope: Internal source/data-flow review only. No new runtime test, no whole-program safety proof, no remote dismissal and no query suppression. Existing host-provided key-quality, entropy health, filesystem and physical erasure assumptions remain separate.
